claims.text: HEA nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
The initial nanoparticles are homogeneous, single-phase solid solutions.
Structural and chemical stability from 473 to 1923 K is governed by a balance between configurational entropy and lattice distortion.
High configurational entropy stabilizes simple, chemically disordered solid-solution phases, particularly at high temperature.
Small atomic-size mismatch allows entropy-driven stabilization to limit atomic diffusion.
Limiting atomic diffusion maintains a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
Significant lattice distortion reduces diffusion barriers and enhances atomic diffusion.
Enhanced diffusion caused by lattice distortion can overcome entropy stabilization.
Diffusion that overcomes entropy stabilization leads to phase segregation or short-range chemical ordering at elevated temperatures.
Lattice distortion arises from atomic-size differences among the constituent metals.
Lattice distortion controls the rate and extent of atomic diffusion.
HEA nanoparticles can exhibit structural similarity and catalytic durability between 573 and 1000 K.
Nanoparticles with minimal atomic-size mismatch will retain a uniform single-phase structure across 473–1923 K.
Nanoparticles with minimal atomic-size mismatch will retain stable catalytic or thermoelectric performance across 473–1923 K.
Nanoparticles with larger atomic-size mismatches will develop secondary phases or compositional inhomogeneity during thermal treatment.
Phase changes or compositional inhomogeneity will be accompanied by catalytic or thermoelectric performance degradation.
Extremely long exposures or temperatures near 1923 K may destabilize even entropically stabilized HEA nanoparticles.
The lattice-distortion threshold for segregation varies with the particular combination of metals.
Low- and high-lattice-distortion nanoparticle sets can be compared under identical thermal cycling, atmospheric, and processing conditions.

Indistinguishable retention of homogeneous single-phase structures and comparable performance in both sets over the full temperature range would falsify the proposed role of lattice-distortion-mediated diffusion.
